criteria.reasoning: Several issues (public safety, data loss, professional integrity, competitive pressure, revenue) are described and linked to engineering design and organisational context; stakeholders are explicitly listed. Treatment of each stakeholder's interest is brief rather than deep, so Very good rather than Excellent.

technical_issues.where: DICUSSION: To Ship or Not to Ship
technical_issues.issue: Competitive-advantage claim ('outpacing Samsung and Google') is supported only by a CNBC article on iPhone release psychology; evidence does not clearly substantiate the claim.

technical_issues.where: DICUSSION: To Ship or Not to Ship
technical_issues.issue: No quantitative evidence anywhere in the report (no defect rates, failure likelihood, cost/fine figures).
EACE clause 2.3b is about competence/qualifications, not resource constraints on testing; misapplied.
Item 3 is internally inconsistent: it advises a longer cycle 'until they have the resources to achieve a six-month product cycle', though the six-month cycle was the stated problem.
Reference [3] has no URL and [4] has garbled author names; IEEE style applied inconsistently and reference list is very short.
Grammar errors: 'have her company might go under'; 'The economic benefits of could very well be' (missing word).

overall: A coherent, well-structured ethics report with balanced arguments, relevant case studies and a justified 'do not ship' recommendation. Limited by sparse references, no figures or quantitative evidence, a few grammatical slips and some misapplied ethical-code clauses.
